correctness.rationale: For K=R or C, Y nonzero arbitrary Banach and 0<=lambda<1, the defect D(a,y)=sqrt((|a|^p+||y||^p)^(2/p)-lambda²|a|²) (max norm for p=infty) is a norm precisely when lambda=0 or p=2 or (1<p<2 and lambda²<=(p-1)2^(2/p)/p). Necessity reduces by restricting to a real scalar+unit vector plane; sufficiency uses coordinatewise monotonicity of an absolute convex plane norm to lift to arbitrary Y and complex scalars. For 1<p<2, the 1/2-Hessian B of (x^p+y^p)^(2/p) has determinant (p-1)S^(4/p-2)x^(p-2)y^(p-2); the Schur complement gives t<=q_p(r), whose derivative changes sign exactly at r=1. The global minimizer c_p is attained there, including endpoint. Continuous C1 gluing across axes and convexity of the quadratic restriction to them yield global convexity of G; its square-root gauge is a norm. For t>c_p the v=(1,-(2-p)/p) direction has negative Hessian at (1,1), ruling out convex square of a norm. p=1 triangle counterexample, p>2 midpoint counterexample (because h^p=o(h²)), p=infty and p=2 explicit. Independently reproduced the exact p=3/2 Schur threshold and negative witness algebra.
